newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: LITHUANIA - GDP GREW BY 3.6 PERCENT IN 1996.
newsitem.headline: LITHUANIA - GDP GREW BY 3.6 PERCENT IN 1996.

text.p: Lithuania's statistics department said on Friday that preliminary data suggested the country's gross domestic product (GDP) grew by 3.6 percent in 1996 in current prices.
The department said in a statement that the country's GDP in current prices, which takes inflation into account, rose to 31.115 billion litas in 1996 from 23.829 billion litas in 1995.
In constant (1993) prices, GDP rose from 11.551 billion litas to 11.963 billion litas, the department said.
It added that its preliminary data suggested that the country's GDP in the last quarter of last year also grew by 3.6 percent or almost 8.6 billion litas.
The department said that the private sector accounted for 68 percent of Lithuania's GDP in 1996 compared with 65 percent in 1995.
It also said that the economy's fastest growing areas were in agriculture, industry, construction and trade.
The department said that the figures would be revised after agricultural partnerships and small enterprises submitted reports on their economic activities for 1996.
The Lithuanian government says it expects GDP growth of five percent this year.
The country's economy began growing in 1994 after a sharp slump sparked by the collapse of its trading ties with the former Soviet Union and the elimination of key subsidies, especially for fuel.
The country's GDP contracted by 34 percent in 1992 and economic activity declined a further 32 percent in 1993, the statistics department said.
